claims.text: Solidified FeNiCrMn has a Co-free composition.
The dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn is governed by thermally activated dislocation glide.
Temperature systematically influences thermally activated dislocation glide in FeNiCrMn.
Strain rate systematically influences thermally activated dislocation glide in FeNiCrMn.
Dislocation density mediates the response of FeNiCrMn to changes in temperature and strain rate.
Grain-boundary structure mediates the response of FeNiCrMn to changes in temperature and strain rate.
The yield strength of FeNiCrMn increases with strain rate.
The ductility of FeNiCrMn increases with strain rate.
The yield strength of FeNiCrMn decreases with temperature.
The ductility of FeNiCrMn decreases with temperature.
FeNiCrMn may transition to a different deformation mechanism at high temperatures or low strain rates.
The proposed hypothesis applies from -200°C to 600°C.
The proposed hypothesis applies from strain rates of 10^-3 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1.
Temperature and strain rate should be varied systematically while yield strength, ductility, dislocation density, and grain-boundary structure are measured.
Failure to observe the predicted temperature and strain-rate correlations would falsify the hypothesis.
Observation of a different deformation mechanism would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome permits a transition to a different deformation mechanism at high temperature or low strain rate, whereas the falsification rule says that observing a different mechanism would falsify the hypothesis without exempting that predicted transition.
